standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting a coherent sheaf along a union of two smaller closed supports
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-prepare-filter-support (invoked at proof line 2704)
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the short exact sequence $0 \to \mathcal{G}_1 \to \mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{G}_2 \to 0$ with supports in the two strictly smaller closed pieces, which condition (1) turns into a contradiction.

standard_prerequisites.name: A power of the ideal of the support annihilates the sheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf (invoked at proof lines 2721 and 2762)
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives $\mathcal{J}^n\mathcal{F} = 0$ for the ideal defining the reduced structure on the support, and later it kills the kernel of the comparison map supported away from the open $V$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Preparation of a sheaf by powers of an ideal sheaf, via Artin-Rees
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, labels lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible (invoked at proof line 2741) and lemma-Artin-Rees (invoked at proof line 2764)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first produces the injective maps $\mathcal{I}_1^{\oplus r_1} \to \mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{I}_2^{\oplus r_2} \to \mathcal{G}$ with cokernels supported in proper closed subsets and hence the open $V$ over which $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ become isomorphic after taking powers; the second makes the resulting map injective after increasing the exponent.

standard_prerequisites.name: Maps defined over an open extend after multiplying by a power of the ideal of the complement
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-homs-over-open (invoked at proof line 2755)
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the map $\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{G}^{\oplus r_1} \to \mathcal{H}^{\oplus r_2}$ which is an isomorphism over $V$.

standard_prerequisites.name: Coherent modules on a closed subspace are pushforwards of coherent modules on it
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, label spaces-morphisms-lemma-i-star-equivalence (invoked at proof line 2738) and Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-coherent-support-closed (invoked at proof line 2739)
standard_prerequisites.use: Together they express $\mathcal{F} = i_*\mathcal{H}$ with $\mathcal{H}$ coherent on the closed subspace $Z$ defined by $\mathcal{J}$, which is what allows condition (3) to be applied.

core_obligations: Assume the collection of closed supports of counterexamples is nonempty and choose a minimal one $T$, using that $|X|$ is Noetherian (proof lines 2680-2699).

Rule out a reducible $T = Z_1 \cup Z_2$ by writing $\mathcal{F}$ as an extension of sheaves supported on the strictly smaller $Z_i$, both of which satisfy $\mathcal{P}$ by minimality, and applying condition (1) (proof lines 2701-2714).

Rule out the case where the ideal $\mathcal{J}$ of the reduced structure on the irreducible $T$ does not annihilate $\mathcal{F}$: filter $\mathcal{F}$ by the powers of $\mathcal{J}$, whose successive subquotients are annihilated by $\mathcal{J}$, and reduce by condition (1) to the case $\mathcal{J}\mathcal{F} = 0$ (proof lines 2716-2731).

In the remaining case, write $\mathcal{F} = i_*\mathcal{H}$ and use condition (3) together with the preparation lemmas to find ranks $r_1, r_2$ and a nonempty open $V$ over which $\mathcal{H}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ agree up to powers; extend the resulting map over $V$ to an injective map $\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{G}^{\oplus r_1} \to \mathcal{H}^{\oplus r_2}$ with cokernel supported in $Z \setminus V$, using Artin-Rees for injectivity (proof lines 2733-2763).

Conclude the contradiction: condition (3)(b) gives $\mathcal{G}'$ with $\mathcal{P}$ and an injection $(i_*\mathcal{G}')^{\oplus r_1} \to \mathcal{F}^{\oplus r_2}$ with proper closed cokernel, so condition (1) and minimality give $\mathcal{P}$ for $\mathcal{F}^{\oplus r_2}$, and condition (2) gives it for $\mathcal{F}$ (proof lines 2764-2775).
proof_roadmap: The injection $\mathcal{I}^n\mathcal{G}^{\oplus r_1} \to \mathcal{H}^{\oplus r_2}$ over the open $V$ (proof lines 2733-2763).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a criterion reducing a property of coherent sheaves on a Noetherian algebraic space to its behaviour on supports: two out-of-three for short exact sequences, descent from finite direct sums, and a supply of sheaves on every reduced irreducible closed subspace, together force the property for all coherent sheaves (statement lines 2651-2677). The proof picks a minimal counterexample support, rules out reducible supports by an extension argument, filters away the powers of the ideal of the support, and in the irreducible case compares the given sheaf with the sheaf supplied by condition (3) over a nonempty open, extending the comparison by Artin-Rees and finishing with conditions (1) and (2). The minimal-counterexample reduction and the comparison over an open are the substance, so the claim is H2.
